transcription.warning: HUMAN_VERIFIED — approved by the repository owner (@marinoscar) on 2026-09-02 (issue #212, PR #214). Basis of approval, recorded precisely so a later reader can judge its weight: the 128 questions, the 8 categories and every static answer were transcribed from the text layer of the official USCIS document M-1778 (09/25), “128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version)”, downloaded 2026-09-02 from the sourceUrl above, with provenance.sha256 recording the exact bytes read; the transcription was then checked by re-parsing that same source text with an independent parser and diffing every prompt, every static answer and every senior-eligible flag against this file, which reported zero mismatches and independently derived the same 20 asterisked questions. The owner reviewed and approved that record. This was an owner sign-off on a machine transcription plus an automated source diff — it was NOT an independent page-by-page human re-read of the PDF, and this note says so rather than implying a stricter check than the one performed. Three things a later reviewer should still weigh: (1) the 8 dynamic questions (Q23, 29, 30, 38, 39, 57, 61, 62) never carry an invented officeholder name. The source itself prints no name for them, so they carry the source’s own answer instead — the “Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates…” instruction for the four national officeholders, and “Answers will vary” guidance scoped to the learner’s state for the state-scoped ones (including the source’s definite answers for D.C. and the territories: no U.S. senators, a nonvoting Delegate or Resident Commissioner, no governor for D.C.). Their verifiedAt stays null and they are NOT certified by this status: the current officeholder is operational data maintained through PUT /api/civics/dynamic-answers (issue #217). (2) Q62's 56 per-state capitals are not from the source document; each such row's own sourceNote discloses that. (3) Q39 (Vice President) and Q57 (Chief Justice) are dynamicScope “national” here, a deliberate divergence from civics-2008.json's “none” scoping, because the 2025 source defers both to testupdates — not an inconsistency to “fix”.
